data.narrative:
Planet Labs operates in Space & Aerospace at the public market stage, competing within a universe of 5 public-market and 8 private-market comparables. The peer set spans established launch providers (SpaceX at $1.6T, Rocket Lab at $40.0B) alongside smaller orbital and Earth-observation specialists (Firefly Aerospace at $2.9B, Astroscale at $840M), creating a notably wide valuation dispersion.

The peer-median method is applicable and yields a primary valuation anchor. Across the four same-sector, same-stage comparables, the median valuation is $21.4B, with a range spanning $840M to $1.6T. A public-comp anchoring approach using Space & Aerospace P/S multiples (median 24.4x across six sector tickers) cannot be applied, as Planet Labs' revenue is not disclosed in the provided data.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $18.2B to $24.7B (median $21.4B). This range reflects the peer-median method's output with symmetrical sensitivity bands. Key uncertainties include the extreme dispersion within the comparable set—a 1,905x gap from Astroscale to SpaceX—which limits precision. The applicability of early-stage space venture valuations to a now-public company, and the absence of revenue-based multiples, further constrain confidence in point estimates. Current market valuation of $7.56B sits substantially below this peer-anchored range.
